Zero-Tool 3D Inverse Folding Benchmark

Can language models design sequences for 3D protein shapes?

Trace2Fold tests inverse folding: we give a language model a table of 3D coordinates for a protein backbone (no protein name, no code tools, one reply) and ask for an amino-acid sequence predicted to fold into that shape.

Author: Jacob Vogan (@jvogan) · MIT License · github.com/jvogan/trace2fold

Explore benchmark results Inspect 6 public 3D starter shapes Try reply validator
Each prompt gives alpha-carbon (Cα) positions and outward side-chain directions with no amino-acid labels. Independent folding models predict the 3D shape of the reply and compare it with the target.
24 holdout shapes
12 matched A/B pairs at 48, 80, 112, and 176 residues, plus 20 public starter shapes (6 viewable in 3D).
14 LLMs and 5 baselines
Single-turn model settings compared against 2 simple controls (shuffle, 1D helix/strand/coil rule) and 3 specialist design tools.
2 folding models + 1 check
Sequence-only ESMFold2-Fast and Boltz-2 average, verified by Apple SimpleFold 3B (rank correlation ρ = 0.987 and 0.969).
Matched A/B twin pairs
Each pair shares chain length and similar helix/strand/coil labels (≥ 70%; 66.5% on the 176-aa beta pair) to test real 3D design.

Scoring and baselines

How Composite Fit (0–100) and Twin Δ grade 3D design

How do you grade a designed sequence? First, two independent folding models (ESMFold2-Fast and Boltz-2) predict what 3D shape the sequence actually forms from its letters alone. Then Composite Fit averages three geometry checks, and Twin Δ checks whether the sequence matches this exact shape rather than a similar decoy.

Backbone match (40% weight)

Rotates and aligns the predicted chain once onto the target, then counts how many alpha-carbons land within 0.5, 1, 2, and 4 Å. Allowing rotations only blocks mirror-image folds, and four distance cutoffs stop one loose end from ruining the score the way raw RMSD does.

Technical term: Single-fit proper-Kabsch coverage at GDT-HA cutoffs (0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0 Å, det(R) = +1).

Local distances (25% weight)

Compares pairwise distances between nearby alpha-carbons (within 15 Å and more than one position apart in sequence) across 0.5, 1, 2, and 4 Å tolerances with no whole-chain alignment. Accurate helices, strands, and turns still earn credit even if a flexible hinge tilts two regions.

Technical term: Superposition-free Cα lDDT over pairs within 15 Å at sequence separation |i − j| > 1.

Long-range contacts (35% weight)

Checks whether residues at least 6 positions apart in sequence pack within 8.0 Å inside the 3D core without forming false contacts. Open unfolded chains miss real contacts (low recall), wrong compact blobs add false ones (low precision), and this term drives 46.8% of score variance across the 14 LLMs.

Technical term: Nonlocal Cα Contact F1 for pairs within 8.0 Å at sequence separation |i − j| ≥ 6.

Zero points for predictor confidence (pLDDT and pTM)

Folding models rate their own confidence per residue (pLDDT) and per chain (pTM), and often give high marks to generic alpha-helices that miss the target shape. Giving confidence 0% weight, averaging two predictors, and checking 10,000 weight tweaks (median rank correlation ρ = 0.9912) keeps rankings tied to 3D geometry.

Twin Δ checks whether the sequence fits this exact shape

Does the sequence fold into this shape, or any shape with the same pattern of helices and strands? Every target A has a hidden twin B with the same length and matching 1D helix/strand/coil labels but a different 3D fold. Subtracting the decoy score gives Twin Δ = Fit(A) − Fit(B).

Observed score scale across baselines and frontier models

7–9 pts · Random floor Shuffled sequence. Keeps amino-acid counts fixed and scrambles order; Twin Δ ≈ 0.0.
10–17 pts · 1D pattern floor 1D H/E/C rule. Picks typical helix, strand, and coil letters using zero 3D coordinates; Twin Δ ≈ +1.5.
46–57 pts · Leading LLMs Single-turn, zero-tool language models. Recovers some 3D arrangement of helices and strands; Twin Δ reaches +37.0.
91–93 pts · Specialist tools Cα-ProteinMPNN, Vanilla ProteinMPNN, and RFD4-Proteina. Under 1.0 Å Cα RMSD on most shapes.

Key findings and scope

What these results show about frontier language models

Across 24 held-out shapes, 3 folding models, and 318 folded LLM sequences (242 in Stage 1 and 76 in Stage 2), five patterns show what language models already handle in 3D and where accuracy breaks down.

Leading models favor the assigned 3D shape over its 1D twin

A model guessing from 1D helix, strand, and coil labels scores almost equally on both shapes in a matched twin pair. At seed 0, the 1D H/E/C control averages Twin Δ of +1.46 in Stage 1 and +1.79 in Stage 2, whereas leading LLMs reach +37.01 and +35.71, showing real 3D target preference.

Long-range core contacts drop off at 176 residues

Models place nearby residues accurately but lose track of distant chain pairings as chains grow longer. Across 318 folded LLM sequences (242 in Stage 1, 76 in Stage 2), recall for distant contacts (≥ 48 positions apart) trails short-range recall by 28.1 and 30.0 points on ESMFold2-Fast (25.1 and 23.6 on Boltz-2), with 0/84 tight ≤ 2.0 Å hits at 176 aa.

A 40-point gap separates specialist tools and zero-tool LLMs

Even when restricted to one backbone point per residue (the alpha-carbon, omitting nitrogen, carbonyl carbon, and oxygen atoms), graph neural network Cα-ProteinMPNN averages 91.56 across all 24 shapes (23/24 within ≤ 2.0 Å Cα RMSD). The top zero-tool LLM setting averages 51.89, leaving a 40-point gap that widens at 176 aa.

Side-chain direction columns help some models and hurt others

Adding three outward side-chain direction columns (dx, dy, dz) tells models which residues face the buried core or outer water, at the cost of a wider numeric table. In paired Stage 1 tests, those columns raised Gemini 4 Carbon High (+20.08) and Neon High (+19.05), lowered GPT-6.2 Sol High (-15.13), and lifted GPT-6.2 Astra High by +9.43 at 176 aa.

More reasoning compute helps models escape helical defaults

Raising test-time reasoning from High to XHigh lifted Gemini 4 Hydrogen by +10.48 points (12/18 shapes), GPT-6.2 Sol by +10.13 (12/18), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 by +6.55 (13/18). On five-strand beta-sheet 48-01-b, Sol High fell back to alpha-helices (4.18), whereas Sol XHigh formed four hairpin turns to score 71.16 (+66.98 points).

What Trace2Fold measures and where it stops

  • Synthetic single-chain targets (24 shapes, 12 twin pairs). The 24 primary holdout shapes come from computer-generated RFD4-Proteina single-chain backbones, supplemented by 4 independent Genie 3 backbones in the generator check, rather than natural multi-domain, cofactor-bound, or multi-chain protein complexes.
  • Computational refolding proxy, not wet-lab assays. Agreement across ESMFold2-Fast, Boltz-2, and SimpleFold 3B tests whether independent folding models predict the target 3D shape from sequence alone, not wet-lab expression, solubility, or folding free energy (ΔG).
  • Prompt versions across stages. Stage 1 (18 shapes at 48, 80, and 112 residues) used prompt v4.2, whereas Stage 2 (6 shapes at 176 residues) and the Genie 3 check used prompt v4.3 with the exact same coordinate format and an explicit single-line output rule.
  • Private holdouts to prevent data leaks. Holdout coordinates stay private so they do not enter training sets. You can run locally on the 20 public gen-* shapes or open a GitHub issue with model settings to request a holdout run.
Methodology and verification checks

Weight stability, coordinate ablations, and independent checks

Four independent checks test whether rankings hold across 10,000 scoring-weight changes, whether models transfer to coordinate-only prompts and a second backbone generator, whether a third folding model agrees, and whether holdout shapes match known Protein Data Bank structures.

Rankings hold across 10,000 weight changes (median ρ = 0.9912)

Do the default 40 / 25 / 35 scoring weights cherry-pick the winner? Across 10,000 weight changes within ±15 points of the defaults, the 14-model ranking stays nearly identical (median rank correlation ρ = 0.9912, minimum 0.9824), and the same three Gemini 4 settings stay top-3 in 100% of random weight combinations.

Those top three settings finish in a statistical tie on this 24-shape panel: testing all 4,096 ways to flip the 12 twin pairs gives p = 0.925 to 0.988 among them. All three lead #4 GPT-6.2 Sol XHigh by +9.49 to +9.75 points (exploratory, unadjusted).

Structural similarity screen across 324,204 known protein chains

To check that holdout shapes are not memorized natural proteins, we screened every target against the January 2025 PDB100 Protein Data Bank snapshot (324,204 known chains) using Foldseek prefiltering and exact US-align 3D shape matching (TM-score, where 1.0 is an exact match).

    Protocol, tools, and attribution
    
Evaluation protocol, benchmark tools, and BibTeX

    

      The public trace2fold repository ships under the MIT License with 20 public gen-* starter shapes, 4 Protein Data Bank calibration structures, coordinate-free score archives in benchmarks/, and offline verification checks. For a reference repository showing how to run the cited folding and structural-biology tools, see BioSymphony/structure-factory.
    


    

      
How the 14 model settings and 5 baselines are evaluated

      

        Each of the 14 model settings pairs a model identifier with its provider reasoning effort (High, XHigh, or Max). Every target runs in a fresh single-turn session with code execution, web search, and file tools disabled, alongside 5 reference controls (2 simple baselines and 3 specialist tools). SHA-256 prompt and target fingerprints live in benchmarks/stage-one-scores.json and benchmarks/stage-two-scores.json.
      

      

        The deterministic length-aware-v2 parser extracts an exact-length sequence of the 20 standard amino-acid letters (replies without a match score 0.00). Each sequence is folded from its letters alone (no sequence alignments or structural templates) across random seeds 0–4 on ESMFold2-Fast and Boltz-2, plus seed 0 on Apple SimpleFold 3B. See CONTRIBUTING.md to test locally or request a holdout run.
